nuggets.title: Silent feature drift before labels arrive

scenario.symptoms: Checkout conversion looks stable in business dashboards, but fraud block rate dropped 18% over two weeks. Ground-truth chargeback labels lag 30 days, so model accuracy charts still show green.
scenario.interviewerSetup: The team only monitors precision/recall after label joins complete. A mobile app release changed how device fingerprints are encoded, shifting live feature distributions without triggering infra alerts.

incident.headline: Monitoring waits on delayed labels while live feature drift goes undetected

agenda.goal: Detect covariate shift on live inputs before ground-truth labels arrive.
agenda.opener: Business metrics moved but model accuracy still looks fine—what broke in monitoring, and how would you catch this earlier?

evidence.strong: Compares live feature distributions to a training baseline with PSI/KL on prioritized features, alerts on drift, and ties to model version and cohort dimensions.
evidence.adequate: Mentions watching input features but without baseline comparison or statistical tests.
evidence.weak: Relies only on delayed label-based accuracy or generic latency/error metrics.

misconceptions.pattern: Comparing today’s traffic only to yesterday’s traffic.
misconceptions.challenge: Gradual drift over weeks can look normal day-to-day—what is the stable reference?

probes: Which features would you monitor first given hundreds of columns?
How do you separate a real drift from a holiday traffic mix shift?
hints: Think about what the model was trained on.
Population Stability Index compares distributions to a reference.
agenda.referenceFix: Run scheduled PSI (or KL) against training baselines on top features and prediction score distributions; alert before label joins; slice by model version and app version to localize the bad release.

scenario.symptoms: PagerDuty fired 400 alerts in one hour after a minor deployment. Most cohorts have fewer than 50 events per day, and static thresholds were copied from the global dashboard.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Each country × product × model version slice has its own threshold. Low-volume cohorts breach constantly on noise, while the global metric still looks healthy.

incident.headline: Static per-cohort thresholds create alert fatigue on sparse slices

agenda.goal: Scale alerting across high-cardinality cohorts without drowning operators in false positives.
agenda.opener: On-call got hundreds of pages after a small deploy—how would you redesign alerting for thousands of cohorts?

evidence.strong: Uses anomaly detection or dynamic baselines, minimum sample size gates, hierarchical rollups, and alert grouping/deduping.
evidence.adequate: Suggests raising thresholds or muting low-traffic cohorts without a systematic policy.
evidence.weak: Manually configures static thresholds for every cohort slice.

probes: How do you alert on a cohort with 10 events per day?
When should a child cohort roll up to a parent alert?
hints: Sparse counts make fixed thresholds noisy.
Seasonal baselines beat one global cutoff.
agenda.referenceFix: Gate alerts on minimum volume, use automated baselines/anomaly detection per tier, rollup rare cohorts to parent dimensions, and dedupe correlated pages into one incident.

nuggets.title: Analysts query raw PII in prediction logs

scenario.symptoms: Security review flagged that model monitoring logs store full billing addresses and emails. A data analyst exported 2M rows for drift analysis without field-level restrictions.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Logging was added quickly at inference time with the full request payload. RBAC exists on dashboards but the warehouse table is wide open to the analytics role.

incident.headline: Sensitive inference payloads land in analytics storage unredacted

agenda.goal: Minimize and protect sensitive fields in monitoring data while keeping drift signals.
agenda.opener: Monitoring logs exposed PII to analysts—where should privacy controls live in this pipeline?

evidence.strong: Redacts or tokenizes PII at ingestion, logs only features needed for drift, applies column-level ACLs, retention limits, and sampling.
evidence.adequate: Masks fields in the BI tool but leaves raw tables queryable.
evidence.weak: Assumes all engineers and analysts may read full payloads.

misconceptions.pattern: Masking only in the dashboard UI.
misconceptions.challenge: What stops someone from querying the warehouse directly?

probes: Do you need 100% of payloads to compute PSI on categorical features?
Where is the earliest safe point to strip emails and addresses?
hints: Clean at the source before durable storage.
Hashing stable identifiers can preserve joins without exposing PII.
agenda.referenceFix: Redact/tokenize PII in the inference logging agent, store hashed user keys and numeric features for drift, enforce warehouse column ACLs, shorten retention, and sample high-cardinality text fields.
